title: The dwarf planets, in order from the Sun
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: In 2006 astronomers created a new group, the dwarf planets, for round worlds that orbit the Sun but have not cleared their path of other objects. Pluto is the most famous; one sits in the asteroid belt and the rest are far beyond Neptune.

How to hold it: Five fits in one chunk. Make a first-letter sentence for the order (C, P, H, M, E), for example "Curious Penguins Hike Many Evenings," or better, one of your own. Then give each a picture from its fact: a cereal bowl for Ceres, a heart for Pluto, a spinning football for Haumea, and a goddess with a single moon for Eris.
